title: OSAPHLA · Spanish
subtitle: Spanish for English speakers
description: An accessible, 36-week, 180-section, offline-first Spanish course targeting an ILR 2 core with ILR 2+/2+/2 stretch preparation.
disclaimer: Course scores and speaking feedback are formative and do not constitute an official ILR rating.

readingAssignments.label: Reading activity 1
readingAssignments.title: How Spanish Works: Main idea
readingAssignments.passage: Ana abre su cuaderno. Escucha una palabra, marca la sílaba fuerte y la repite. No busca la perfección; busca una mejora clara cada día.
readingAssignments.passageTranslation: Ana opens her notebook. She listens to a word, marks the stressed syllable, and repeats it. She is not seeking perfection; she seeks one clear improvement each day.
readingAssignments.instructions: Read once for the overall situation. Read again and state the main idea in one sentence without translating every word.
prompts: Who or what is this passage mainly about?
What is the central action or situation?

sections.subtitle: concept and objective framing
sections.grammar: Noun gender and number; definite and indefinite articles; hay; classroom commands.
sections.pronunciation: Final consonants, especially s; contrast singular and plural without adding an English vowel.

content.heading: Operational objective
content.body: By the end of this section you can identify people and objects, ask what something is, follow basic instructions. The focus is useful performance, not isolated terminology.

content.heading: Language system
content.body: Noun gender and number; definite and indefinite articles; hay; classroom commands.

content.heading: Sound and delivery
content.body: Final consonants, especially s; contrast singular and plural without adding an English vowel.

content.heading: Core principle
content.body: Notice meaning first, then form. Retrieve the new language aloud, compare it with the model, and repair one feature at a time.

content.heading: Gender is part of the noun
content.body: Every Spanish noun has grammatical gender. Learn the article and noun as one unit: la palabra, not just palabra; el libro, not just libro. Grammatical gender is a word category and does not necessarily describe sex or identity.

content.heading: The four definite articles
content.body: Use el with a masculine singular noun and la with a feminine singular noun. Their plurals are los and las: el libro → los libros; la palabra → las palabras.

content.heading: Indefinite articles
content.body: Un and una mean a or an; unos and unas mean some. They must match the noun: un libro, una mesa, unos libros, unas mesas.

content.heading: Patterns are clues, not guarantees
content.body: Nouns ending in -o are often masculine, while -a, -ción, -sión, and -dad are often feminine. These are useful clues, not rules without exceptions: el día, el problema, and la mano must be learned with their articles.

content.heading: Agreement across the phrase
content.body: Articles, nouns, and descriptive adjectives agree in gender and number: un libro nuevo, una palabra nueva, los libros nuevos, las palabras nuevas. Some adjectives, such as importante, use the same singular form for both genders.

¿Qué es esto?
Es una pregunta importante.
Abran los cuadernos, por favor.
Las respuestas están en la página diez.

Model set. El banco está entre la farmacia y la tienda. Hay una silla al lado de la mesa. Los libros están encima del escritorio. No hay nadie dentro de la oficina. Estamos fuera del edificio. The bank is between the pharmacy and the store. There is a chair next to the table. The books are on top of the desk. There is no one inside the office. We are outside the building.

Contrastive practice. Change the person, time, number, or level of formality in each model. Preserve the communicative purpose while the grammar changes.

Production check. Say one original sentence for each function: locate a place; describe a temporary condition; say what is available. Then write it and compare the spoken and written forms.

content.heading: Operational objective
content.body: By the end of this section you can describe people and relationships, express possession, identify a person precisely. The focus is useful performance, not isolated terminology.

content.heading: Language system
content.body: Adjective agreement and position; possessive adjectives and pronouns; tener; personal a.

content.heading: Sound and delivery
content.body: Diphthongs and smooth linking across word boundaries.

content.heading: Core principle
content.body: Notice meaning first, then form. Retrieve the new language aloud, compare it with the model, and repair one feature at a time.

content.heading: Adjectives agree
content.body: A variable adjective matches the noun in gender and number: un amigo alto, una amiga alta, unos amigos altos, unas amigas altas. The noun controls the form of the adjective.

content.heading: Not every adjective changes for gender
content.body: Adjectives ending in -e or many consonants commonly keep one singular form: un amigo amable and una amiga amable. They still change for plural number: amigos amables, amigas amables.

content.heading: Position affects emphasis
content.body: Descriptive adjectives usually follow the noun. Some common adjectives can appear before it, sometimes with a change in emphasis or form. First secure agreement; then learn position as part of each expression.

modelSentences: Mi hermana mayor es muy amable.
Conozco a los padres de Elena.
Nuestra familia vive en tres ciudades.
¿Es suyo este retrato?
Tengo dos hermanos y una prima.
modelTranslations: My older sister is very kind.
I know Elena's parents.
Our family lives in three cities.
Is this portrait yours?
I have two brothers and one female cousin.

My friend is tall and nice. The students are hardworking. The students are hardworking. She is intelligent and patient.

Contrastive practice. Change the person, time, number, or level of formality in each model. Preserve the communicative purpose while the grammar changes.

Production check. Say one original sentence for each function: describe people and relationships; express possession; identify a person precisely. Then write it and compare the spoken and written forms.

Adjectives agree. A variable adjective matches the noun in gender and number: un amigo alto, una amiga alta, unos amigos altos, unas amigas altas. The noun controls the form of the adjective.

Not every adjective changes for gender. Adjectives ending in -e or many consonants commonly keep one singular form: un amigo amable and una amiga amable. They still change for plural number: amigos amables, amigas amables.

Position affects emphasis. Descriptive adjectives usually follow the noun. Some common adjectives can appear before it, sometimes with a change in emphasis or form. First secure agreement; then learn position as part of each expression.

content.body: Applying the form. Use acabar de + infinitive for something just finished, tener que + infinitive for obligation, and ir a + infinitive for near-future plans.

content.heading: Production check

content.heading: Form and meaning
content.body: Applying the form. Combine si + present tense with another present or near-future clause to describe a likely condition and its result: si llueve, cambiamos el plan.

content.heading: Model set
content.body: Hace sol hoy, pero va a llover mañana. Si llueve, cambiamos el plan. Está nublado en la montaña. Hace mucho frío en la costa. Si hace calor, vamos a la playa.
content.translation: It's sunny today, but it's going to rain tomorrow. If it rains, we change the plan. It's cloudy in the mountains. It's very cold on the coast. If it's hot, we go to the beach.

content.heading: Contrastive practice

content.heading: Form and meaning
content.body: Applying the form. Some verbs use an irregular future stem (haré, tendré, podré) instead of the infinitive; the future tense can also express present probability: estará en casa (he's probably home).

content.translation: I will do the homework tomorrow. I will have time next week. I will be able to help you later. He/she is probably home now. He/she is probably about thirty.

content.heading: Contrastive practice

content.heading: Form and meaning

content.heading: Form and meaning
content.body: Applying the form. Use the indicative in a relative clause when the antecedent is known/specific, and the subjunctive when it's unknown or hypothetical: conozco a alguien que tiene (known) vs. busco a alguien que tenga (unknown).

content.heading: Model set
content.body: Busco a alguien que tenga experiencia. Conozco a la persona que tiene experiencia. El lugar donde vivo es tranquilo. Necesito algo que funcione bien. Uso lo que ya tengo.
content.translation: I'm looking for someone who has experience. I know the person who has experience. The place where I live is quiet. I need something that works well. I use what I already have.

content.heading: Contrastive practice
content.body: Change the person, time, number, or level of formality in each model. Preserve the communicative purpose while the grammar changes.

media.transcript:
Form and meaning. Applying the form. Use the indicative in a relative clause when the antecedent is known/specific, and the subjunctive when it's unknown or hypothetical: conozco a alguien que tiene (known) vs. busco a alguien que tenga (unknown).

Model set. Busco a alguien que tenga experiencia. Conozco a la persona que tiene experiencia. El lugar donde vivo es tranquilo. Necesito algo que funcione bien. Uso lo que ya tengo. I'm looking for someone who has experience. I know the person who has experience. The place where I live is quiet. I need something that works well. I use what I already have.

Contrastive practice. Change the person, time, number, or level of formality in each model. Preserve the communicative purpose while the grammar changes.

Production check. Say one original sentence for each function: define a requirement; identify known and unknown people or things; connect complex information. Then write it and compare the spoken and written forms.

content.heading: Form and meaning
content.body: Applying the form. Use había + participle for an action completed before another past event, and aunque + indicative for a known concession (aunque hay) vs. aunque + subjunctive for a hypothetical one.

content.heading: Model set
content.body: El cambio ya había ocurrido antes del informe. Según se afirma, la reforma amplió derechos. Aunque hay consenso, el debate continúa. A pesar de que hay evidencia, algunos dudan. La consecuencia fue inmediata.
content.translation: The change had already occurred before the report. As is claimed, the reform expanded rights. Although there is consensus, the debate continues. Despite there being evidence, some doubt it. The consequence was immediate.

content.heading: Contrastive practice

content.heading: Read for the situation
content.body: Al terminar el curso, la meta no es saber cada palabra. La meta es comprender, actuar, reparar errores y seguir aprendiendo. La competencia se mantiene con contacto frecuente y tareas cada vez más exigentes.
content.translation: At the end of the course, the goal is not to know every word. The goal is to understand, act, repair errors, and keep learning. Proficiency is maintained through frequent contact and increasingly demanding tasks.

content.heading: Cultural lens
content.body: Intercultural competence means observing, asking, adapting, and avoiding claims that one community represents all speakers.

content.heading: Avoid the single-story trap
content.body: Treat country, region, age, relationship, and setting as variables. Describe the evidence you have without turning one example into a universal rule.

content.heading: Language variation
content.body: Recognize regional choices and ask what a form means locally. Use the neutral course model for production until the situation gives you a reason to adapt.

content.heading: Reflection
content.body: Compare this context with one you know. Name one similarity, one difference, and one question that would prevent an assumption.

readingAssignments.passage: Al terminar el curso, la meta no es saber cada palabra. La meta es comprender, actuar, reparar errores y seguir aprendiendo. La competencia se mantiene con contacto frecuente y tareas cada vez más exigentes.
readingAssignments.passageTranslation: At the end of the course, the goal is not to know every word. The goal is to understand, act, repair errors, and keep learning. Proficiency is maintained through frequent contact and increasingly demanding tasks.
readingAssignments.instructions: Read once for the overall situation. Read again and state the main idea in one sentence without translating every word.
prompts: Who or what is this passage mainly about?
What is the central action or situation?
Summarize the passage in one English sentence, then try one Spanish sentence.
